96	open CategoryTheory
97	
98	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
99	
100	namespace Scheme
101	
102	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
103	
104	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
105	
106	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
107	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
108	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
109	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
110	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
111	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
112	
113	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
114	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
115	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
116	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
117	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
118	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
119	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
120	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
121	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
122	
123	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
124	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
125	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
126	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
127	sieve on the underlying scheme.
128	
129	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
130	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
131	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
132	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
133	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
134	  intro T S hS
135	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
136	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
137	
138	namespace PicSharp
139	
140	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
141	
142	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
143	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
144	
145	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
146	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
147	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
148	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
149	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
150	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
151	
152	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
153	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
154	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
155	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
156	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
157	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
158	
159	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
160	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
161	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
162	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
163	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
164	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
165	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
166	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
167	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
168	
169	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
170	
171	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
172	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
173	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
174	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
175	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
176	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
177	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
178	
179	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
180	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
181	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
182	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
183	  (etaleSheaf C).property
184	
185	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
186	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
187	
188	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
189	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
190	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
191	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
192	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
193	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
194	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
195	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
196	
197	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
198	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
199	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
200	
201	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
202	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
203	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
204	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
205	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
206	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
207	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
208	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
209	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
210	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
211	
212	end PicSharp
213	
214	namespace PicScheme
215	
216	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
217	
218	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
219	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
220	forgotten,
221	
222	```
223	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
224	```
225	
226	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
227	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
228	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
229	`picSharp`.
230	
231	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
232	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
233	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
234	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
235	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
238	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
239	
240	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
241	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
242	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
243	
244	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
245	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
246	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
247	the name is not available here). -/
248	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
249	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
250	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
251	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
252	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
253	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
254	
255	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
256	
257	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
258	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
259	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
260	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
261	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
262	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
263	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
264	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
266	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
267	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
268	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
269	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
270	  exact h
271	
272	end PicScheme
273	
274	end Scheme
275	
276	end AlgebraicGeometry

module

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.DescentData

/-!
# Stacks: effectiveness of descent

Let `C` be a category with a Grothendieck topology `J` and `F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat`.
In this file, we define the typeclass `F.IsStack J` saying that `F` is a stack for `J`.
(See the terminological note in the file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/IsPrestack.lean`:
we do not require that the categories `F.obj (.mk (op S))` are groupoids.)

The typeclass `IsStack` extends `IsPrestack`. The effectiveness of descent that
is required for stacks is expressed by saying that the functors `toDescentData`
attached to covering sieves are essentially surjective. Together with the
`IsPrestack` assumption, we get that these functors are actually equivalences of
categories (see `isEquivalence_toDescentData`). Conversely, we provide a
constructor `IsStack.of_isStackFor` which assumes that these functors are
equivalences of categories.

## References
* [Jean Giraud, *Cohomologie non abélienne*][giraud1971]
* [Gérard Laumon and Laurent Moret-Bailly, *Champs algébriques*][laumon-morel-bailly-2000]

-/

public section

universe t t' v' v u' u

namespace CategoryTheory

open Bicategory

namespace Pseudofunctor

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- The property that a pseudofunctor `F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat`
has effective descent for a Grothendieck topology, i.e. is a stack.
(See the terminological note in the introduction of the file
`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/IsPrestack.lean`.) -/
@[stacks 026F]
class IsStack (F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat.{v', u'}) (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Prop
    extends F.IsPrestack J where
  essSurj_of_sieve (F) {S : C} (R : Sieve S) (hR : R ∈ J S) :
    (F.toDescentData (fun (f : R.arrows.category) ↦ f.obj.hom)).EssSurj

variable (F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat.{v', u'}) {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

/-- Version of `isStackFor` for a sieve instead of a presieve. -/
lemma isStackFor' [F.IsStack J] {S : C} (R : Sieve S) (hR : R ∈ J S) :
    F.IsStackFor R.arrows := by
  rw [isStackFor_iff]
  have hF := (F.isPrestackFor' _ hR).fullyFaithful

/-!
# Faithfully flat descent for modules

In this file we show that extension of scalars by a faithfully flat ring homomorphism is comonadic.
Then the general theory of descent implies that the pseudofunctor to `Cat` given by extension
of scalars has effective descent relative to faithfully flat maps (TODO).

## Notes

This contribution was created as part of the AIM workshop
"Formalizing algebraic geometry" in June 2024.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u

noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory Comonad ModuleCat Limits MonoidalCategory

variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] {f : A →+* B}

lemma ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_tensorLeft_of_ringHomFlat (hf : f.Flat) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits <| tensorLeft ((restrictScalars f).obj (ModuleCat.of B B)) := by
  algebraize [f]
  change PreservesFiniteLimits <| tensorLeft (ModuleCat.of A B)
  infer_instance

lemma ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat (hf : f.Flat) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (extendScalars.{_, _, u} f) := by
  have : PreservesFiniteLimits (extendScalars.{_, _, u} f ⋙ restrictScalars.{_, _, u} f) :=
    ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_tensorLeft_of_ringHomFlat hf

/-- Extension of scalars along faithfully flat ring maps reflects isomorphisms. -/
lemma ModuleCat.reflectsIsomorphisms_extendScalars_of_faithfullyFlat
    (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat) : (extendScalars.{_, _, u} f).ReflectsIsomorphisms := by
  refine ⟨fun {M N} g h ↦ ?_⟩
  algebraize [f]
  rw [ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective] at h ⊢
  replace h : Function.Bijective (LinearMap.lTensor B g.hom) := h
  rwa [Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective] at h

/-- Extension of scalars by a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
def comonadicExtendScalars (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat) :
    ComonadicLeftAdjoint (extendScalars f) := by
  have := preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat hf.flat
  have := reflectsIsomorphisms_extendScalars_of_faithfullyFlat hf
  convert!
    Comonad.comonadicOfHasPreservesFSplitEqualizersOfReflectsIsomorphisms
      (extendRestrictScalarsAdj f)
  · exact ⟨inferInstance⟩
  · exact ⟨inferInstance⟩

364	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0DualNumberCocycle

/-!
# The relative Picard group at a one-point test object (A.3.iii, tangent lane)

At a test object `T` whose underlying space is a **single point** — for the tangent-space
computation the two cases are the dual numbers `Spec k[ε]` and the base `Spec k` itself —
the coset subgroup `π_T^* Pic(T)` that the *relative* Picard functor quotients out is
**trivial**, so

```
Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)  ≃+  Pic(C ×_k T).
```

The coset calculus of `PicSharp.relPresheaf` therefore disappears from the ε-kernel
computation entirely, and the dual-number kernel of the *relative* functor may be computed
on the *absolute* Picard group, where the two-chart Čech model of
`Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean` §6 lives.

## Why this is cheap

`IsLocallyTrivial` asks for an affine open `U ∋ x` trivialising the module. On a one-point
space *every* nonempty open is `⊤`, so a locally trivial module is **globally** trivial and
no cover-splitting argument is needed. That is the whole content: the collapse is
**topological**, not commutative algebra about `Pic` of an Artin local ring.

The general-coefficient statement ("`Pic` of a finite product of Artin local rings
vanishes") is true, is genuine commutative algebra, and is *not needed here*.

## Main declarations

* `LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.trivial_of_subsingleton` — a locally trivial module on a
  one-point scheme is trivial. Scheme-general, no hypothesis on the module beyond local
  triviality.
* `PicSharp.relPicRel_iff_iso_of_subsingleton` — at a one-point test object the `H_T`-coset
  relation *is* the absolute iso-class relation, in both directions.
* `PicSharp.relPicQuotAddEquivAbs` — the resulting additive equivalence
  `Pic(C ×_S T)/π_T^* Pic(T) ≃+ Pic(C ×_S T)`, with the computation rule
  `PicSharp.relPicQuotAddEquivAbs_mk`.

Cross-project note: the sibling `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` has the same collapse
on its own carrier (`Tangent/RelPicPointTest.lean`, `picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton`),
where the relative group is a `QuotientGroup` by an honest subgroup and the argument is five
lines on top of `CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`. This project's carrier is a *setoid*
quotient of `LineBundle.OnProduct` with no subgroup to name, so the collapse has to be proved
at the level of the relation — which is what the second declaration above does. The two are
the same mathematics on different carriers (inbox I-0495, 2026-07-28).

Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §2 `df:Pfs`, §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020).
-/

/-!
# Zariski descent of representability (`thm:representability_zariski_descent`)

This file proves **Zariski descent of representability** (EGA 0_I 4.5.4;
cf. Stacks 01JJ): a presheaf `F : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1` satisfying the Zariski
sheaf axiom (`Scheme.IsZariskiSheafOver`, stated against open covers of the
total space of each `T : Over S`) that is representable over every member of
an open cover of `S` is representable by an `S`-scheme
(`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`).

The definitions `overRes` / `overResHom` / `overResLE` / `IsZariskiSheafOver`
and the statement of the descent theorem previously lived in
`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean` (where the theorem was a typed `sorry`
leaf); they are moved here so the Grassmannian file can consume the proof.

## Proof architecture

The heavy gluing content (cocycle conditions, `Scheme.GlueData`, the
locally-bijective sheaf comparison) is **not** redone by hand: it is delegated
to mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy`
(Stacks 01JJ), which applies to a `Type 0`-valued Zariski *sheaf* on the
absolute category `Scheme.{0}` equipped with a jointly surjective family of
relatively representable open immersions from representables.  The work done
here is the translation layer:

1. **Size reduction / total functor** (`ZariskiDescent.GluedPoint`,
   `ZariskiDescent.gluedFunctor`): the values of `F` live in `Type 1`, so `F`
   cannot be fed to the mathlib theorem directly.  Instead we encode a point
   of the would-be total space over `T : Scheme` as a `Type 0` datum: a base
   morphism `a : T ⟶ S` together with a family of *classifying morphisms*
   `γ i : T|_{a⁻¹ U i} ⟶ Y i` into the local representing objects, compatible
   on overlaps as classified `F`-sections.  The bespoke sheaf axiom for `F`
   shows `GluedPoint T ≃ Σ (a : T ⟶ S), F(T, a)` (`ZariskiDescent.totalEquiv`),
   identifying `gluedFunctor` with the (large) total functor of `F`.
2. **Sheaf axiom** (`ZariskiDescent.isSheaf`): `gluedFunctor` is a sheaf for
   the big Zariski topology.  Covers by arbitrary jointly surjective open
   immersions are reduced to covers by opens of the target (the generated
   sieves agree), where the claim follows from the sheaf axiom of `F` through
   `totalEquiv`.
3. **Charts** (`ZariskiDescent.chart`): each `Y i` maps to `gluedFunctor` by
   sending `t : T ⟶ (Y i).left` to the point classified by the `F`-section
   that `t` represents; these are relatively representable open immersions
   (the pullback against a point `(a, x)` of `gluedFunctor` is the open
   subscheme `a⁻¹ U i ⊆ T`) and jointly surjective.
4. **Conclusion**: mathlib glues a scheme `Ŷ` with `gluedFunctor ≅ Hom(-, Ŷ)`;
   the tautological point of `Ŷ` gives the structure morphism `â : Ŷ ⟶ S`,
   and `totalEquiv` converts the absolute representability into
   `F.RepresentableBy (Over.mk â)`.
